After the last freeze, walk the whole line and push on each post. Any movement means the footing has heaved or the post has begun to rot at grade. Let new cedar or pressure-treated wood weather three to six months before the first coat. Fresh lumber carries mill glaze and moisture that will not let a finish penetrate, and sealing too early traps that moisture inside the board. After the first coat, plan on cleaning and re-sealing every two to three years in this climate — sun-facing runs may need it sooner than shaded ones.

Pressure washing can strip years off a wood fence if it is done wrong. Stay under 1,500 PSI, use a wide fan tip, keep the wand moving and hold it at least a foot off the surface. Anything more aggressive gouges the soft grain and leaves a fuzzy, splintered face that will not take a finish evenly.
